tagline: Thailand's last province on the eastern coast, home to Koh Chang, Koh Kood, and Koh Mak — clear water and quiet seas
introHtml:
Trat is the easternmost province, right up against the Cambodian border, about a 4–5 hour drive from Bangkok. Most people come here to catch a boat out to the islands, because this is where you'll find Koh Chang, one of the largest islands in the country, Koh Kood with its clear water and calm, and Koh Mak, a small island that's still easygoing.

Beyond the sea, the town itself has an old quarter along Bang Phra Canal, a morning market, and old Chinese shrines to wander. Down south there are small beaches around Khlong Yai and the Ban Hat Lek border market next to Cambodia. When fruit season comes around April to June, the orchards here produce durian, rambutan, and mangosteen just like the neighbouring provinces. If you like a quiet sea without the crowds, Trat is the kind of destination plenty of people travel a long way to reach.
bestTime: November–April, when the sea is clear and calm — good for island-hopping and diving. In the rainy season from June to September many islands are quiet and some places close.

highlights.name: Koh Chang
highlights.blurb: The province's big island, with white-sand beaches, Kai Bae Beach, jungle waterfalls, and a wide range of places to stay from bungalows to resorts. The boat across from Ao Thammachat pier is short.

highlights.name: Koh Kood
highlights.blurb: Trat's furthest island, with very clear water and quiet beaches. There's Khlong Chao Waterfall and the Takian Thong wooden bridge — an island where people come to settle in for a calm, longer stay.

highlights.name: Koh Mak
highlights.blurb: A small island in the middle of the Trat sea, flat enough to get around by bike, with clear water and quiet beaches. Good for an easy stay with no fuss.

highlights.name: Trat Old Town along Bang Phra Canal
highlights.blurb: An old community in the heart of town with wooden houses, Chinese shrines, coffee shops, and local food along the canal to stroll past.

highlights.name: Ban Hat Lek border market
highlights.blurb: The southernmost point of the province, a Thai–Cambodian border crossing with a market and border food to stop for before you reach the edge of the country.

highlights.name: Koh Chang's beaches and waterfalls
highlights.blurb: Koh Chang has white-sand beaches, Sai Daeng Beach, Sapparot Bay, plus Khlong Phlu and Than Mayom waterfalls in the forest at the centre of the island.

foodScene.name: Seafood by the sea
foodScene.note: The whole province sits on the coast, with seafood spots on the islands and along the shore — crab, prawns, shellfish, squid, and fresh fish straight off the local boats.

foodScene.name: Dried seafood and Khlong Yai shrimp paste
foodScene.note: Trat is known for shrimp paste, fish sauce, dried squid, and dried shrimp — especially Khlong Yai shrimp paste, which people buy to take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Noodles and food in town
foodScene.note: In Trat town there are noodle shops, rice-and-curry stalls, and morning market food to try before you head out to the islands.

foodScene.name: Durian, rambutan, mangosteen
foodScene.note: In fruit season around April to June, the orchards in Trat produce durian, rambutan, and mangosteen, sold at stalls and markets all over town.

foodScene.name: Local sweets and souvenirs
foodScene.note: Trat has crispy tang me toffee, rice crackers, and processed snacks made from fruit and seafood, sold at souvenir shops in town.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town and on the islands
foodScene.note: The old quarter along Bang Phra Canal and the islands of Koh Chang and Koh Kood have cafes and coffee shops with sea views to sit and take a break.

foodScene.name: Grilled seafood by the beach
foodScene.note: On the islands and along the beaches there are grilled seafood spots — grilled prawns and squid — to sit down for dinner by the sea.

attractions.name: Koh Chang
attractions.blurb: A big island with several beaches, jungle waterfalls, and hiking trails — the province's main sea destination.

attractions.name: Koh Kood
attractions.blurb: The furthest island, clear and quiet, with Khlong Chao Waterfall and white-sand beaches for an easygoing stay.

attractions.name: Koh Mak
attractions.blurb: A small, flat island you can explore by bike, with clear water and quiet beaches — good for a relaxed stay.

attractions.name: Khlong Phlu Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A large waterfall in the forest at the centre of Koh Chang. You can walk in and swim in the clear pool — the island's best-known waterfall.

attractions.name: Old Town along Bang Phra Canal
attractions.blurb: An old community in the heart of Trat town — wooden houses, Chinese shrines, cafes, and local food along the canal to stroll past.

attractions.name: Wat Buppharam
attractions.blurb: Trat's oldest temple, with a museum of antiques and well-preserved wooden architecture.

attractions.name: Ban Hat Lek border market
attractions.blurb: The country's southernmost Thai–Cambodian border crossing, with a market and border food to look around.

attractions.name: Koh Chang Naval Battle Memorial
attractions.blurb: A memorial to the naval battle with France at Laem Ngop, with a seaside museum telling the history.

itineraryIdeas: Trat 3D2N — Laem Ngop and Koh Chang
